description.narrative:
Röda khmertribunalen (formellt "Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia", ECCC) påbörjade sin verksamhet 2006 efter överenskommelse mellan FN och Kambodjas regering. Det huvudsakliga syftet med domstolen är att lagföra seniora röda khmerledare för brott mot nationell och internationell lagstiftning begångna under perioden för Demokratiska Kampuchea mellan åren 1975 till 1979. De samlade brotten inbegriper bland annat ansvaret för uppskattningsvis två miljoner människors död. Domstolen är central både för att framhäva vikten av lagstyre samt för andra processer som relaterar till försoning, lag och rätt i landet. Flertalet enskilda organisationer och personer inom civila samhället kan, med ECCC som utgångspunkt, driva frågor som i vid bemärkelse relaterar till domstolens arbete, vilket annars skulle försvårats betydligt. Enbart genom sin existens har domstolen därmed hjälpt till att lyfta en rad frågor om Röda khmerernas tid vid makten och det lidande de orsakade till allmän diskussion.
Domstolen är ett internationellt åtagande till vilket Sverige tidigare lämnat stöd. Det föreslagna svenska stödet avser bidrag för perioden 2016 till 2023 och är av stor vikt för domstolens möjlighet att slutföra båda delmålen i fall 002 samt, om förundersökningarna så visar, avsluta rättegångar i fall 003 och 004. Insatsen bygger på två tidigare svenska bidrag till domstolen mellan 2012 och 2015 uppgående till totalt SEK 58 miljoner (se avsnitt 2b i "Appraisal of Intervention, final" för närmare detaljer).

The contribution constitutes support to the Khmer Rouge tribunal in Cambodia. Committed funds will support the international part of the Court in its running costs. The mandate of the Court is to try the main culprits from the former regimes leadership for crimes committed during 1975-1979.

To bring the most senior and responsible leaders of the Khmer Rouge regime to trial for crimes committed during the period of Democratic Kampuchea and to enhance domestic judicial reform through capacity building and transfer of knowledge and know-how from the ECCC to the national justice system.

Since case 003 and 004 where terminated by the court in 2021, case 002/02 regarding Khieu Samphan, was the only proceeding in 2022. On 23 December 2022, the Supreme Court Chamber notified its written judgment on the appeals in case 002/02. In concluding judicial work, the Supreme Court Chamber upheld Khieu Samphans convictions for genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity in the Case 002/02 Appeals Judgment. The decision marks the first time in which a national appeals court upheld a genocide conviction against a former head of state. This filing completed appeal proceedings in case 002/02. Case 002 is the first case tried by an internationalized tribunal that was severed into two trials for case management purposes. When Khieu Samphan was sentenced by the Trial Chamber to life imprisonment in Case 002/02, after having already been sentenced to life imprisonment in Case 002/01, the Supreme Court Chamber had to clarify whether he serves a single life sentence or two life sentences that run concurrently. The Supreme Court Chamber explained that Khieu Samphan serves a single life sentence, which is the maximum sentence permitted under Cambodian law. Under the ECCCs Internal Rules, the CoProsecutors are responsible for initiating and implementing the enforcement of sentences, in cooperation with the national authorities. Before the Case 002/02 Appeals Judgment was issued, the CoProsecutors began discussions with the General Department of Prisons of the Cambodian Ministry of the Interior to identify an appropriate detention facility for Khieu Samphan, since he was sentenced to life imprisonment in Case 002/01. The Kandal Provincial Prison was selected, and the CoProsecutors made multiple trips to the prison to confirm that it met with Cambodian and international standards, which require that Khieu Samphans advanced age and fragile state of health be considered when making detention arrangements. On 30 January 2023, Khieu Samphan was transferred to the Kandal Provincial Prison to continue to serve his life sentence. The International Committee of the Red Cross carries out regular visits to monitor conditions and treatment. Following the Appeals Judgment, the Supreme Court Chamber is responsible for reviewing the security classifications of all documents on the case file, and declassifying documents where a confidential classification is no longer necessary. A similar process is underway in Case 004/02. Reclassification is a crucial part of the ECCCs legacy. A Working Group for VictimsSurvivor Initiatives during the Residual Phase of the ECCC was constituted on 10 October 2022, comprising personnel of the ECCC, civil society organizations and others working with victim survivors of the Khmer Rouge regime. The objective of the crosscutting Working Group is to deliver appropriate initiatives that promote reconciliation, healing, intergenerational dialogue and education, as part of the residual phase of the ECCC. Following the completion of Case 002, the ECCC is working to notify Civil Parties across the country about the case through focal points and provincial meetings. The ECCC returned its compound to the Royal Cambodian Army Headquarters and officially relocated to its residual premises in central Phnom Penh on 29 December 2022, and commenced it's residual functions on 1 January 2023. The new premises serves as a hub for the ECCC to disseminate information about the ECCC's work of the past 16 years. It hosts a public and freely accessible Resource Centre and will soon complete works on an international standard archive repository. In 2023 the ECCC additionally became a member of the International Council on Archives (ICA) and now partner with many local and international institutions and associations through MoUs. The development of a modern and interactive legacy website is also underway. Once completed, the new website will shift the way users approach and research the history of the Khmer Rouge and the ECCC. These facilities and resources help in making the work and the legacy of the ECCC more accessible to the public. It can also function as a resource for professionals within the Cambodian justice system, as well as current and future international/hybrid courts.
